messages.author: 97942d52cc45a8f1
messages.subject: Extending a run
parts:
I would like to write some code that automatically extends a chain.

I start with something like:
fit1 <- stan("MyModel.stan",data=my.data,
                  inits=my.inits,
                  chains=n.chains,iter=n.sample+n.warmup,
                  warmup=n.warmup)


suppose I now look at n_eff and I find that it is smaller than I want, so I define a new target length.
n_eff <- monitor(fit1,print=FALSE)[,"n_eff"]
newiter <- round(n.sample*min(max(1,n_eff.min/min(n_eff)),10))



where n_eff.min is the minimum acceptable value of n_eff.

So now I do a second run, something like:
  fit2 <- stan(fit=fit1,data=my.data,
                  inits=new.inits,
                  chains=n.chains,iter=newiter+n.warmup,
                  warmup=n.warmup)


I have several problems with this construction.
1) RStan doesn't seem to remember and reuse elements for the previous fit.  This doesn't work at all if I don't supply the data argument. If I leave off the number of chains, it returns to the RStan default of 4 (I prefer 3, but that is personal taste).  This behavior seems different from how other R functions like lm behave when starting from a previous fit.

2) It seems like RStan redoes the warmup.  This is a waste of time, as I was already happy with the previous warmup values.  It also produces a discontinuity if I try to paste the two results together. (see 4).

3) How do I set new.inits?  I could reuse my.inits, but I would prefer to start from where I left off.  The output of as.matrix seems ill suited to this purpose, as inits is looking for a list.

4) What I would really like to do is to combine the samples from fit1 and fit2 (as they are both ideally samples from the same posterior distribution).  For some purposes, I can just use rbind(as.matrix(fit1),as.matrix(fit2)), but for others I would like to keep this as a stanfit object so I can use the RStan methods.  Simply adding them in as new chains using sflist2stanfit won't work because the chains are of unequal length.

Thanks in advance for any advise you can give.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Extending a run
parts: On May 20, 2014, at 2:48 AM, Russell Almond <alm...@acm.org> wrote:

> I would like to write some code that automatically extends a chain.
>
> I start with something like:
> fit1 <- stan("MyModel.stan",data=my.data,
> inits=my.inits,
> chains=n.chains,iter=n.sample+n.warmup,
> warmup=n.warmup)
>
>
> suppose I now look at n_eff and I find that it is smaller than I want, so I define a new target length.
> n_eff <- monitor(fit1,print=FALSE)[,"n_eff"]
> newiter <- round(n.sample*min(max(1,n_eff.min/min(n_eff)),10))
You might want to leave a little leeway if you really need that minimum.

> where n_eff.min is the minimum acceptable value of n_eff.
>
> So now I do a second run, something like:
> fit2 <- stan(fit=fit1,data=my.data,
> inits=new.inits,
> chains=n.chains,iter=newiter+n.warmup,
> warmup=n.warmup)
>
>
> I have several problems with this construction.
> 1) RStan doesn't seem to remember and reuse elements for the previous fit. This doesn't work at all if I don't supply the data argument. If I leave off the number of chains, it returns to the RStan default of 4 (I prefer 3, but that is personal taste). This behavior seems different from how other R functions like lm behave when starting from a previous fit.

Correct. You need to pass it the last sample from the previous
fit as the init. Then it'll have to go through warmup again, because
we aren't saving the warmup info in a way that we can read it back in.

Also, if you don't have enough effective samples, you sometimes need to
run warmup longer. So we just suggest re-running from scratch with more
iterations (double is a good heuristic).

>
> 2) It seems like RStan redoes the warmup. This is a waste of time, as I was already happy with the previous warmup values. It also produces a discontinuity if I try to paste the two results together. (see 4).

That's the piece we need to add --- we don't have a way to say start
from the previous warmup values. But it is on our short-term to-do list,
so we hope to get to it soon.
> 3) How do I set new.inits? I could reuse my.inits, but I would prefer to start from where I left off. The output of as.matrix seems ill suited to this purpose, as inits is looking for a list.
That's an R question I don't know the answer to.

>
> 4) What I would really like to do is to combine the samples from fit1 and fit2 (as they are both ideally samples from the same posterior distribution). For some purposes, I can just use rbind(as.matrix(fit1),as.matrix(fit2)), but for others I would like to keep this as a stanfit object so I can use the RStan methods. Simply adding them in as new chains using sflist2stanfit won't work because the chains are of unequal length.

You really need to concatenate them onto the end of the last chains.

Another issue on our refactoring the commands list is to deal with
R-hat and n_eff calculations with unequal chain sizes. We don't right
now. There are two obvious, but different ways to do this --- average
by chain or average by sample. So this one's going to take some research.

- Bob

Glad to see this is on the to do list.

>> 3) How do I set new.inits?  I could reuse my.inits, but I would prefer to start from where I left off.  The output of as.matrix seems ill suited to this purpose, as inits is looking for a list.

> That's an R question I don't know the answer to.

The essence of the problem here is that the data structures are different.  In my specific example, I have parameters "pi", "mu" and "sigma" which are all IxK matrices.  The as.matrix/as.array functions return these as a vector of length IK.  I suppose I could do something like:
new.inits <- vector("list",n.chains)
for (c in 1:n.chains) {
 new.inits[[c]] <- lapply(level1.params,
                         function (param) {
                           arr <- as.array(fit1,pars=param)
                           last <- dims(arr)[1]
                           matrix(arr[last,c,],my.data$I,my.data$K)
                         })
names(new.inits[[c]]) <- level1.params

The problem is that this code doesn't generalize very well.  I have level2.params as well which have different dimensions.  It would be nice if somehow the stanfit object could keep information about the dimensions of parameters to make this kind of transformation easier.

>
>> 4) What I would really like to do is to combine the samples from fit1 and fit2 (as they are both ideally samples from the same posterior distribution).  For some purposes, I can just use rbind(as.matrix(fit1),as.matrix(fit2)), but for others I would like to keep this as a stanfit object so I can use the RStan methods.  Simply adding them in as new chains using sflist2stanfit won't work because the chains are of unequal length.

> You really need to concatenate them onto the end of the last chains.

I can do this fairly easily if i'm just extracting data; I can just use rbind as above.  However, the plot and traceplot methods require a stanfit object.  Not sure how that would work.  (Maybe I'm better off moving to coda here).

> Another issue on our refactoring the commands list is to deal with
> R-hat and n_eff calculations with unequal chain sizes.  We don't right
> now.  There are two obvious, but different ways to do this --- average
> by chain or average by sample.    So this one's going to take some research.

If I'm appending to the end of the chains, shouldn't this just be as if I have longer chains, or is the discontinuity going to do something strange to the autocorrelation estimates?
- Bob

Thanks,
  --Russell

The information's there in the stanfit object, at least
in its C++ linkage to the model, which has all that information.
Again, I'm not sure what the easiest way to convert a sample to
a valid input is, but Ben or Jiqiang may have a one-liner up their
sleeve or a pointer to existing doc.

>
>
> >
> >> 4) What I would really like to do is to combine the samples from fit1 and fit2 (as they are both ideally samples from the same posterior distribution). For some purposes, I can just use rbind(as.matrix(fit1),as.matrix(fit2)), but for others I would like to keep this as a stanfit object so I can use the RStan methods. Simply adding them in as new chains using sflist2stanfit won't work because the chains are of unequal length.
>
> > You really need to concatenate them onto the end of the last chains.
>
> I can do this fairly easily if i'm just extracting data; I can just use rbind as above. However, the plot and traceplot methods require a stanfit object. Not sure how that would work. (Maybe I'm better off moving to coda here).

You can recreate a Stan fit object from chains. You'll lose
some of the info attached to the model, but for analysis, it'll
do what you need.

I think Martyn updated Coda to use the same R-hat as we're using.
I don't know about the n_eff calcs --- we use cross-chain information
to help estimate means, but I think that's unusual.

>
> > Another issue on our refactoring the commands list is to deal with
> > R-hat and n_eff calculations with unequal chain sizes. We don't right
> > now. There are two obvious, but different ways to do this --- average
> > by chain or average by sample. So this one's going to take some research.
>
> If I'm appending to the end of the chains, shouldn't this just be as if I have longer chains, or is the discontinuity going to do something strange to the autocorrelation estimates?

You should only append if it's a single Markov chain. Otherwise,
you're right that it'll mess up n_eff calculations, which are
based on autocorrelation estimates. They should ideally just go
in separate chains, but we don't support that for different sized chains
yet (at least I don't think we do --- Daniel's been building the code
out in this area lot recently so it may be coming soon).

- Bob

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: RStan: converting sample to appropriate input or data?
parts:
On Tuesday, May 20, 2014 6:01:21 PM UTC-4, Bob Carpenter wrote:
> The problem is that this code doesn't generalize very well.  I have level2.params as well which have different dimensions.  It would be nice if somehow the stanfit object could keep information about the dimensions of parameters to make this kind of transformation easier.

The information's there in the stanfit object, at least
in its C++ linkage to the model, which has all that information.
Again, I'm not sure what the easiest way to convert a sample to
a valid input is, but Ben or Jiqiang may have a one-liner up their
sleeve or a pointer to existing doc.

library(rstan)
funnel <- stan_demo("funnel")
inits <- apply(funnel, 2, relist, skeleton = rstan:::create_skeleton(funnel@model_pars, funnel@par_dims))
funnel <- stan(fit = funnel, init = inits)

I think create_skeleton() is being exposed in the next rstan so you won't have to do the :::

Ben
